text:
Anika: Customer report — FinApps (enterprise) says after our v9.2 rollout their assistant responses are 'more concise, sometimes dropping clarifying questions and examples'. They attached before/after samples and a minimal repro. Not an outage but a UX regression for them.

support-bot: Ticket created: #C-4821. Priority: P2. Link: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/C-4821 :white_check_mark:

Matt: Can you paste the minimal repro here (prompt + params)? Did they move from v9.1 -> v9.2 or was v9.2 a new variant? Was any quantization/compile change applied to that model?

Anika: Repro below (customer used chat endpoint, model 'redwood/v9.2', temperature 0.2, max_tokens 250). Examples:

Customer prompt (shortened): "Write an onboarding email for a new user who signed up for a project management app. Include next steps and one optional tip."

Before (v9.1):
"Hi Jenna — congrats on signing up! To get started, click X, add your first project, invite teammates. Next steps: ... Would you like a checklist or a short walkthrough?"

After (v9.2):
"Hi Jenna — congrats on signing up! Click X and add your first project."

Seems the 'Would you like a checklist...' clarifying question disappeared.

Request sample (redacted):
```json
{
  "model": "redwood/v9.2",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Write an onboarding email for a new user who signed up for a project management app. Include next steps and one optional tip."}],
  "temperature": 0.2,
  "max_tokens": 250
}
```

Sophia: Hmm. That feels like a subtle decode distribution shift. Can you include the customer's API request IDs (req_id) so we can pull logs? Also confirm whether they were routed to dedicated infra or hosted.

Anika: Two request ids: req_9a1b2c and req_9a1b2d. They route to hosted-only. Latency normal (~120ms), no errors. I uploaded full before/after pair to the ticket.

Oliver: Quick triage steps I'd run:
- Re-run the exact request against v9.1 and v9.2 with deterministic settings: `temperature:0.0, top_p:1.0, max_tokens:250` to see if sampling randomness is a factor.
- Run n-gram coverage diff and check attention pattern logs (if we have them).
- Check compile flags and kernel selection logs for v9.2 on the serving nodes that handled those requests.

Matt: If repro holds at temp 0, then it's model-behavioral (weights/param change) not sampling. Could be a changed system prompt or response-length penalty baked into the model variant. I'll ask model-onboarding to confirm if a new safety/verbosity token penalty was introduced.

Anika: Quick test I ran: same request at `temperature:0.0` produced the tighter response on v9.2 as well. Pasting both outputs in ticket.

Matt: Okay that's actionable. Short plan:
1) Matt to ask onboarding/release leads if v9.2 included any response-length priors or prompt edits.
2) ML team to diff deterministic outputs and produce minimal reproducer harness (A/B with v9.1).
3) Support to offer FinApps routing to v9.1 while we investigate.

Anika: FinApps said they'd accept routing to v9.1 for now. I'll set a temporary customer route and confirm.

support-bot: Update: Routing change applied for FinApps — now pinned to redwood/v9.1 for production traffic. Action owner: Anika. :lock:

Sophia: Also add a short eval with 50 varied prompts to quantify average token delta and frequency of missing clarifying follow-ups. I can spin that up if you want.

Matt: Yes please. Sophia, can you share results in this thread when ready? I'll sync with onboarding/release.

Oliver: Adding: if kernel/compile differences are found, we might need an emergency micro-rollback or compile tweak rather than model rollback.

Anika: Thanks — I'll update ticket and loop FinApps. Keeping this thread open for ML findings.
